title: Factors, primes and powers
ks3: Number: factors, multiples, primes, HCF, LCM, powers and roots
intro: Factors, multiples and prime numbers, prime factor trees, HCF and LCM, and squares, cubes and their roots.
description: Free KS3 Maths questions with answers on factors, multiples, prime numbers, prime factorisation, HCF and LCM, squares, cubes and roots. Marked instantly, for Year 7, 8 and 9 (ages 9 to 14).

questions.q: Which of these is a factor of 18?
questions.hint: A factor divides into 18 exactly, with nothing left over.
questions.explain: 18 ÷ 6 = 3 exactly, so 6 is a factor. 4 and 8 leave a remainder, and 36 is a multiple of 18, not a factor.

questions.q: How many factors does 12 have?
questions.hint: List them in pairs that multiply to 12: 1 × 12, 2 × …
questions.explain: The factor pairs are 1 × 12, 2 × 6 and 3 × 4. So the factors are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12: that is 6 factors.

questions.q: What is the highest common factor (HCF) of 24 and 36?
questions.hint: List the factors of each number and find the biggest one in both lists.
questions.explain: Factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. Factors of 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36. The biggest in both is 12.

questions.q: Ali puts 24 apples and 40 oranges into identical fruit bags, with nothing left over. What is the largest number of bags that can be made?
questions.hint: The number of bags must divide both 24 and 40. You want the biggest such number.
questions.explain: This is the HCF of 24 and 40. Factors of 24: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12, 24. Factors of 40: 1, 2, 4, 5, 8, 10, 20, 40. The HCF is 8, so 8 bags, each with 3 apples and 5 oranges.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT a factor of 24?
questions.hint: A factor divides into 24 exactly, with nothing left over.
questions.explain: 6 × 4 = 24, 8 × 3 = 24 and 12 × 2 = 24, so those are factors. 24 ÷ 9 = 2 remainder 6, so 9 is not a factor.

questions.q: What is the highest common factor (HCF) of 18 and 30?
questions.hint: List the factors of 18 and the factors of 30. Which is the biggest number in both lists?
questions.explain: Factors of 18: 1, 2, 3, 6, 9, 18. Factors of 30: 1, 2, 3, 5, 6, 10, 15, 30. The biggest in both lists is 6.

questions.q: Which number is a multiple of 7?
questions.hint: Count up the 7 times table: 7, 14, 21, …
questions.explain: 6 × 7 = 42. The others are not in the 7 times table (57 = 3 × 19).

questions.q: What is the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 4 and 6?
questions.hint: Write out the multiples of each and find the first one in both lists.
questions.explain: Multiples of 4: 4, 8, 12, 16, … Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, … The first in both lists is 12.

questions.q: One bus leaves every 12 minutes and another leaves every 18 minutes. They both leave at 9:00. How many minutes later do they next leave together?
questions.hint: You need the lowest common multiple of 12 and 18.
questions.explain: Multiples of 12: 12, 24, 36, … Multiples of 18: 18, 36, … The LCM is 36, so they leave together again after 36 minutes, at 9:36.

questions.q: Which number is a multiple of both 3 and 4?
questions.hint: Check each number: is it in the 3 times table? Is it in the 4 times table?
questions.explain: 24 = 3 × 8 and 24 = 4 × 6, so 24 is a multiple of both. 16 is only in the 4 times table, 18 is only in the 3 times table, and 14 is in neither.

questions.q: What is the lowest common multiple (LCM) of 6 and 9?
questions.hint: Write out the first few multiples of 6 and of 9. Find the first number in both lists.
questions.explain: Multiples of 6: 6, 12, 18, 24, ... Multiples of 9: 9, 18, 27, ... The first number in both lists is 18.

questions.q: Veggie burgers come in packs of 8 and burger buns come in packs of 12. Tom wants exactly the same number of burgers and buns. What is the smallest number of burgers he can buy?
questions.hint: The number of burgers must be a multiple of 8 and also a multiple of 12.
questions.explain: Multiples of 8: 8, 16, 24, ... Multiples of 12: 12, 24, ... The LCM is 24, so 3 packs of burgers and 2 packs of buns give 24 of each.

questions.q: Which of these is a prime number?
questions.hint: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself.
questions.explain: 29 can only be divided by 1 and 29. The others are not prime: 21 = 3 × 7, 27 = 3 × 9 and 39 = 3 × 13.

questions.q: How many prime numbers are there between 10 and 20?
questions.hint: Check each number from 11 to 19. Even numbers (except 2) are never prime.
questions.explain: The primes between 10 and 20 are 11, 13, 17 and 19. That is 4. (15 = 3 × 5, so it is not prime.)

questions.q: Is 1 a prime number?
options: No, because a prime has exactly two factors and 1 has only one
Yes, because it only divides by 1 and itself
No, because it is too small to be a number
questions.hint: Think about how many factors a prime number must have.
questions.explain: A prime number has exactly two different factors. 1 has only one factor (itself), so 1 is not prime. The smallest prime is 2.

questions.q: Which shows 60 written as a product of prime factors?
questions.hint: Every number in the answer must be prime, and they must multiply to 60.
questions.explain: 60 = 2 × 30 = 2 × 2 × 15 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5 = 2² × 3 × 5. The others use 10, 4 or 15, which are not prime, or multiply to 90.

questions.q: There is only one even prime number. What is it?
questions.hint: Every even number divides by 2. Which even number has only two factors?
questions.explain: 2 has exactly two factors, 1 and 2, so it is prime. Every other even number also divides by 2, so it has more than two factors.

questions.q: What is the smallest prime number that is bigger than 50?
questions.hint: Check 51, 52 and 53 in turn. Try dividing by 2, 3, 5 and 7.
questions.explain: 51 = 3 × 17, so it is not prime. 52 is even. 53 does not divide by 2, 3, 5 or 7 (and 7 × 7 = 49, 8 × 8 = 64), so 53 is prime.

questions.q: 84 = 2² × 3 × 7 and 90 = 2 × 3² × 5. Use these to find the highest common factor (HCF) of 84 and 90.
questions.hint: Find the prime factors that appear in both. Take the smaller power of each.
questions.explain: Both have a 2 (84 has 2², 90 has 2, so take 2) and both have a 3 (take 3). 7 and 5 are not in both. HCF = 2 × 3 = 6.

questions.q: Work out 7²
questions.hint: 7² means 7 × 7.

questions.q: What is the square root of 81?
questions.hint: Which number times itself makes 81?
questions.explain: 9 × 9 = 81, so the square root of 81 is 9.

questions.q: Work out 4³
questions.hint: 4³ means 4 × 4 × 4.

questions.q: What is the cube root of 125?
questions.hint: Which number times itself times itself makes 125?
questions.explain: 5 × 5 × 5 = 125, so the cube root of 125 is 5.

questions.q: Work out 2⁵
questions.hint: Multiply 2 by itself 5 times.

questions.q: Which is bigger: 2⁶ or 6²?
questions.hint: Work out each one.

questions.q: 5³ × 5⁴ = 5ⁿ. What is n?
questions.hint: Write it out: (5 × 5 × 5) × (5 × 5 × 5 × 5). How many 5s?
questions.explain: There are 3 + 4 = 7 fives multiplied together, so 5³ × 5⁴ = 5⁷. When you multiply powers of the same number, add the powers.

questions.q: Work out 10³
What is the square root of 144?
questions.hint: Which number times itself makes 144? Try numbers just above 10.
questions.explain: 12 × 12 = 144, so the square root of 144 is 12.

questions.q: Work out 3² + 4²
questions.hint: Square each number first, then add.

questions.q: The square root of 50 is between two whole numbers next to each other. What is the smaller of the two?
questions.hint: Which square numbers are just below and just above 50?
questions.explain: 7² = 49 and 8² = 64. 50 is between 49 and 64, so √50 is between 7 and 8 (it is about 7.07). The smaller number is 7.
